Macrons

Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

what kind of adjective

also what sort of, what type of, what … like, what was it like

classical

Mart. 12.92.4: sī fīās tū leō, quālis eris?
Traupman 406: what kind of, what sort of, quālis

quālis, quāle

adjective, interrogative and relative, third declension

what kind of? what … like?

As a relative it answers tālis: tālis … quālis, such … as. In an exclamation, “what … !”: quālis erat!, how he looked! (Verg. A. 2.274). The noun is also used: quod genus …? (see “kind”).

Other words

  • cujus modī (cujusmodī) — of what kind?

    genitive of quality · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 15.20.3: cupiō cognōscere iter tuum cujus modī sit (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • dīc mihi, sī fīās tū leō, quālis eris?

    tell me, if you turned into a lion, what kind of lion would you be?Mart. 12.92.4

  • ei mihi, quālis erat, quantum mūtātus ab illō

    ah me, what he looked like! how changed from the man he wasVerg. A. 2.274

  • lupus est homō hominī, nōn homō, quom quālis sit nōn nōvit.

    man is a wolf to man, not a man, when he doesn’t know what sort of man the other is.Plaut. Asin. 495

  • gallīna erat lignea patentibus in orbem ālīs, quālēs esse solent quae incubant ōva

    there was a wooden hen with its wings spread round, as hens have them when they sit on eggsPetr. 33.2

See also kind, such, what.

SourcesLewis & Short: qualis · Lewis & Short: cujusmodi

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 406.
